strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with In-Place Scaling
strategies.desc: Uses 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local scaling/unscaling operations per shard, exactly as in the reference. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + ~14 local ops. Represents the baseline: straightforward structure with no fusion, accepting maximum dispatch overhead but simplest correctness reasoning.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce Buffers Pre-Allocation
strategies.desc: Pre-allocates a single buffer and fuses all per-shard scaling operations into vectorized operations before each all-reduce, eliminating clone() calls. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces + 8 fused scale ops + 7 fused unscale ops. Trades memory layout planning for reduced buffer allocation overhead and potential kernel fusion.

strategies.name: Pipelined Dual-Buffer Overlap
strategies.desc: Uses two alternating buffers to overlap computation of scaling for iteration i+1 with all-reduce communication of iteration i, issuing async all-reduces where possible. Dispatch count: 8 all-reduces (overlapped) + ~14 compute ops. Hides local computation latency behind network latency, trading increased memory footprint for reduced wall-clock time.

strategies.name: Batch-Collapsed Multi-Reduce Single Payload
strategies.desc: Stacks all 8 intermediate states into a single (W*256*8) tensor, performs one large all-reduce, then applies all scaling/unscaling transformations as tensor slicing operations. Dispatch count: 1 all-reduce + ~14 local reshape/slice/scale ops. Trades single large payload (56x larger) for 7 fewer network dispatch overheads.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Stage Reduction Tree
strategies.desc:
Exploits the repetitive scale-reduce pattern by factoring into two stages: first 4 iterations reduce to intermediate state, then final 4 iterations complete. Uses reduce-scatter + all-gather pairs within each stage to halve per-rank payload during reduction phases. Dispatch count: 8 reduce-scatter + 8 all-gather (or similar decomposition). Reduces per-operation bandwidth at cost of doubled collective count.
